key_insight: No-slip stagnation points on solid surfaces impose a universal mixing transition: before a boundary-controlled time scale, solute blobs broaden and decay algebraically, while after it the boundary sets a fixed mixing width and exponential decay.
engineering_relevance: For porous media and surface-contact transport, the result provides a predictive Péclet-number scaling law for when mixing is dominated by fluid stretching versus solid-boundary effects.
method: Analyze transport of thin solute strips/sheets near a generic obstacle and separatrix ending at a stagnation point.
Derive an analytically tractable coupled advection-diffusion theory for upstream stagnation-point mixing.
Validate the asymptotic predictions with numerical simulations.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports quantitative agreement between the theory and numerical simulations, including the crossover time scale t_B ~ Pe^(1/3) and the predicted asymptotic scalings of c_max and width σ.
watch_item: The theory is stated for thin blobs near a single generic obstacle and no-slip stagnation points, so extension to complex geometries or multi-obstacle flows may require additional assumptions.
paper_title: Scalar mixing by stagnation points on solid surfaces
